query: For the paper "LibriVoxDeEn: A Corpus for German-to-English Speech Translation and German Speech Recognition" (arXiv: 1910.07924), answer this question: How is the sentence alignment quality evaluated?
context:
[1] Source: 1910.07924.pdf | Page: 4 | Section: 7. Conclusion
Title: LibriVoxDeEn: A Corpus for German-to-English Speech Translation and German Speech Recognition
The audio-text alignment and text-to-text sen- tence alignment was checked to be of high quality in a man- ual evaluation. A cutoff on a sentence alignment quality score allows to ﬁlter the text alignments further, resulting in a clean corpus of 50, 427 German-English sentence pairs aligned to 110 hours of German speech. A larger version of the corpus, comprising 547 hours of German speech and high-quality alignments to German transcriptions is avail- able for speech recognition.

(2018): 1 Wrong alignment 2 Partial alignment with slightly compositional transla- tional equivalence 3 Partial alignment with compositional translation and additional or missing information 4 Correct alignment with compositional translation and few additional or missing information 5 Correct alignment and fully compositional translation The evaluation of the audio-text alignment quality was con- ducted according to the following 3-point scale: 1 Wrong alignment 2 Partial alignment, some words or sentences may be missing 3 Correct alignment, allowing non-spoken syllables at start or end The evaluation experiment was performed by two anno- tators who each rated 30 items from each bin, where 10 items were the same for both annotators in order to calcu- late inter-annotator reliability.

Title: LibriVoxDeEn: A Corpus for German-to-English Speech Translation and German Speech Recognition
The speech translation data consist of 110 hours of audio material aligned to over 50k parallel sentences. An even larger dataset comprising 547 hours of German speech aligned to German text is available for speech recognition. The audio data is read speech and arXiv:1910.07924v3 [cs.CL] 4 Mar 2020 thus low in disﬂuencies. The quality of audio and sentence alignments has been checked by a manual evaluation, showing that speech alignment quality is in general very high.

Title: LibriVoxDeEn: A Corpus for German-to-English Speech Translation and German Speech Recognition
The sentence alignment quality is comparable to well-used parallel translation data and can be adjusted by cutoffs on the automatic alignment score. answer:
The sentence alignment quality is evaluated manually. Two annotators each rated 30 items from each bin, with 10 items shared between them to calculate inter-annotator reliability [2].

The text (sentence) alignment quality is rated on a 5-point scale used in Kocabiyikoglu et al. (2018), ranging from "wrong alignment" (1) up to "correct alignment and fully compositional translation" (5), with intermediate levels covering partial alignments with compositional translation and varying amounts of additional or missing information [2][5].

The evaluation items are divided into bins based on the hunalign confidence score: Low (−0.3 < x ≤ 0.3), Moderate (0.3 < x ≤ 0.8), and High (0.8 < x), so the manual ratings reflect alignment quality across different automatic confidence ranges [10][2].

Question:
For the paper "LibriVoxDeEn: A Corpus for German-to-English Speech Translation and German Speech Recognition" (arXiv: 1910.07924), answer this question: How is the sentence alignment quality evaluated?

Before writing the final answer:
- Synthesize the passages. Where a configuration exception is stated, describe the main pattern as mainly or predominantly and include the exception in the same sentence. Do not repeat an all/only statement that conflicts with that exception. An exception must change the same property; keep independent design choices separate.
- For why questions, explain each supported mechanism. When comparing alternatives, explicitly state their supported equivalent property and quantities, rather than leaving the equivalence implicit in the phrase instead of.
- Omit unnecessary background and names absent from the passages. Do not repeat the same point or list unasked ablations and implementation details.

original_answer:
The sentence alignment quality is evaluated manually. Two annotators each rated 30 items from each bin, with 10 items shared between them to calculate inter-annotator reliability [2].

The text (sentence) alignment quality is rated on a 5-point scale used in Kocabiyikoglu et al. (2018), ranging from "wrong alignment" (1) up to "correct alignment and fully compositional translation" (5), with intermediate levels covering partial alignments with compositional translation and varying amounts of additional or missing information [2][5].

The evaluation items are divided into bins based on the hunalign confidence score: Low (−0.3 < x ≤ 0.3), Moderate (0.3 < x ≤ 0.8), and High (0.8 < x), so the manual ratings reflect alignment quality across different automatic confidence ranges [10][2].
